blurb:
At almost three years old and 71 pounds of leggy Belgian Malinois mix, Hypnotic is the kind of dog who makes you stop scrolling. He loves his people. Like, really loves his people. He's going to want to be near you, involved in what you're doing, and generally in the loop at all times.

He's housetrained, vaccinated, microchipped, heartworm negative, and already neutered, so the logistics are handled. His activity level is listed as "busy bee" and that about covers it. He needs an owner who actually wants to do stuff with their dog, not one who's hoping for a couch ornament.

He gets a little nervous around new dogs, which is worth knowing upfront. He's not aggressive about it. He just wants proper introductions, not a chaotic dog-park free-for-all. If you have a dog at home who's relatively calm and you're willing to do a slow intro, there's a good chance they'll figure each other out. His comfort with kids isn't known since he came in without much history, so a meet before committing is a smart call.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Stop in during visiting hours to meet him in person.
shelter_hours: Check shelter website for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• High-drive Belgian Malinois mix with an eye-catching name — guaranteed scroll-stopper for newsletter readers
• Unknown history and dog-selectivity suggest he's been passed over, adding urgency to his feature
• Perfect match for active adopters seeking a loyal, engaged companion — aspirational lifestyle appeal

blurb:
She came in calm and obedient, and the shelter staff noticed that right away. Skyelynn is a five-year-old Retriever mix, 51 pounds, and she's still in that early shelter phase where she's taking everything in before she shows you who she really is. That's not a red flag. That's just a dog who's been through a transition and needs a minute.

She's housetrained, good with kids, and her activity level is on the lower end, which is actually great news if you want a dog who'll go for a walk and then be perfectly happy to settle in next to you on the couch. She's not going to demand a five-mile run every morning.

She's a little wary around other dogs, so a home without other pets or one with a very calm, low-key dog would be a better fit than a house with a rowdy pack. She's vaccinated, spayed, microchipped, and heartworm negative, so she's ready to go whenever the right person shows up.

Lewisville Animal Services is at 995 College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours and ask to spend some time with her. She just needs a quiet moment to show you what she's got.
shelter_hours: Check shelter website for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Good with kids, low-activity, and fully vetted — one of the most broadly adoptable profiles in this batch
• Lower ID number relative to peers signals she has likely been at the shelter longer than most, raising urgency
• The 'still showing her true self' narrative creates an emotional hook that invites readers to be her turning point

blurb:
Papas is a five-year-old American Pit Bull Terrier mix sitting at 50 pounds, and he checks a lot of boxes right out of the gate. Housetrained. Good with kids. High energy but not unmanageable. Vaccinated, neutered, microchipped, heartworm negative. The basics are all covered.

He's got a high activity level, so he's going to want real exercise, not just a quick lap around the block. If you've got a yard, or you run, or you've been looking for a reason to actually use that dog park membership, Papas is going to appreciate that more than most. He's the kind of dog who's going to be a great companion if you put in the time with him.

His listing doesn't have a ton of notes on his personality yet, which usually just means he's still warming up to shelter life. What's clear is he came in already housetrained and comfortable around kids, and that tells you something about where he came from. Somebody loved this dog. Now he just needs somebody to love him again.

Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Come by during visiting hours and ask to meet him.

scoring_notes:
• 'Somebody loved this dog' is the single most emotionally compelling line in this entire batch — reprint-worthy
• Lowest intake ID number in the group strongly implies he has been waiting the longest, making his feature urgent
• Pit Bull mix stigma paired with a kid-friendly, housetrained profile challenges reader bias and drives meaningful engagement

blurb:
Her name is Wednesday and she did not choose it by accident. She's four months old and already has opinions. The shelter describes her as a grumpy gus, which honestly, same. Not every cat is going to greet you like a golden retriever, and that's fine.

What she does have going for her: she's a kitten with room to grow into whoever she's going to be, she's good with other cats, and she's already litterbox trained at four months old. She's vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed. The groundwork is all there.

She's not looking for someone who needs constant warmth from day one. She's looking for someone patient enough to let her come around on her own schedule. If you've got another cat at home and a little tolerance for personality, Wednesday might actually be a really good fit. She's at Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy. Walk in during visiting hours and introduce yourself. She may or may not be thrilled to meet you, but that's kind of the whole thing with her.

scoring_notes:
• Quirky 'grumpy kitten' persona is highly shareable and will resonate with personality-driven adopters
• Her need for a patient, cat-experienced home narrows the pool but deepens the right match
• At four months old with no urgency signals, she likely arrived recently and wait time appears short

blurb:
Oliver is six years old and eleven pounds, which means he's a full-grown, settled adult cat who already knows who he is. No more kitten chaos, no mystery personality. What you see is what you get.

The listing is light on details, which sometimes just means he's a straightforward, uncomplicated cat. He's litterbox trained, vaccinated, microchipped, and neutered. He hasn't been around kids, so a quieter home or one with older kids would probably suit him better.

Adult cats like Oliver get passed over a lot because people walk straight to the kittens. But a six-year-old cat is often exactly what a busy household actually needs. He's not going to redecorate your walls at 2am. He just needs a calm spot, some food, and someone who's going to be consistent with him. If that sounds like your place, go meet him. He's at Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy during visiting hours.

scoring_notes:
• Adult cats are statistically the most overlooked — featuring Oliver directly addresses a real adoption gap
• Sparse listing details combined with age suggest he has been quietly waiting while kittens get chosen first
• Zero-effort ownership pitch (calm, settled, no surprises) is a strong hook for busy adult readers

blurb:
Some cats want to be held. Bridgette is not one of those cats, and she will let you know. All four paws stay on the floor, thank you very much. But don't mistake that for being aloof, because this girl is about as affectionate as they come. She rolls around on her back, purring, basically demanding that you stop what you're doing and pay attention to her.

She's a year and a half old, sleek and pretty, and fully into catnip and playtime. She's litterbox trained, already vaccinated, microchipped, and spayed. There's nothing left to do on your end except show up and meet her.

If you want a lap cat who wants to be carried everywhere, Bridgette's probably not your match. But if you want a cat who's warm, playful, and completely comfortable just being near you on her own terms, she's worth a visit. She's at Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy. Just walk in during visiting hours and ask about Bridgette.

• Fully vetted, playful, and affectionate on her own terms — broad appeal to independent-cat lovers
• Personality-forward blurb makes her instantly relatable and memorable for newsletter readers

blurb:
Yasmeen's foster mom says her adopters are going to hit the jackpot. That's not a throwaway line — this is an eight-year-old Lab-Terrier mix who came in a little guarded and, within one day of the Prison Pups training program, had completely settled in. She just needed to know she could trust you. Once she does, she's loyal and loving in that quiet, steady way that senior dogs tend to be.

She's done well with other dogs, including a Boxer she stayed with while her foster was on vacation. She's good with cats, too. She met kids as young as seven and gave them kisses. She does have some protective instincts around her people when strangers come into the home — she's worked on it in training and it's improved a lot, but a family with dog-savvy kids 15 and up is probably the smoothest fit. Her trainer will do a proper introduction either way.

If you've wanted a calm, devoted dog who's already past the chaos years, Yasmeen is worth meeting. She's in a foster home now through Mostly Mutts in Kennesaw. Reach out or stop by to get started.
shelter_hours: Please check mostlymutts.org for current hours
scoring_notes:
• Foster's 'jackpot' quote combined with a one-day trust breakthrough is the strongest emotional hook in the entire candidate pool
• Senior dog who thrives with dogs, cats, and young kids defies the hard-to-place stereotype and delivers a genuinely surprising story
• Eight-year-old Lab mix with protective instincts faces real adoption headwinds, making a newsletter feature the highest-leverage intervention available
